answer: An atlas office assigns each agent one summit to survey. The agent climbs it, sets a small mirror on a numbered peg, and tilts it so the sun flashes the base camp at a fixed hour. The camp logs the flash time and the angle against the atlas page for that summit, and a second climber on the next peak checks the mirror is still there the following morning. A thousand fake names need a thousand summits climbed, a thousand mirrors set and angled, and a thousand flashes logged on time, so one copied page buys nothing.
